sources.title: Filtering | Weaviate Documentation
quotes: An inverted index (similar to a traditional search engine) is used to create an allow-list of eligible candidates.
The index will move along any node's edges normally, but will only add ids to the result set that are present on the allow list.
Weaviate offers an option to automatically switch to a flat (brute-force) vector search when a filter becomes too restrictive.
sources.use: Distinguish metadata candidate generation, graph-result filtering, and an exact-scan query-plan fallback. These are not three new ANN indexes.
sources.version_limit: Versionless live documentation; establishes checked terminology, not historical behavior of every release.

sources.title: How we speed up filtered vector search with ACORN
quotes: we use this approach for small filters (configurable by the flatSearchCutOff parameter)
we decided not to modify the indexing from “vanilla” HNSW.
We only use the two-hop expansion if the connecting node does not pass the filter.
sources.use: A search algorithm can make a real contribution without inventing an index name. The blog's custom query algorithm must not be conflated with the paper's construction variants or our ordinary hnswlib traversal.

sources.title: Indexing | Qdrant Documentation
quotes: The index is also used to accurately estimate the filter cardinality, which helps the query planning choose a search strategy.

When the maximum estimated amount of points that a condition satisfies is smaller than full_scan_threshold_kb, the query planner will use full-scan search instead of HNSW index traversal for better performance.
Qdrant solves this problem by extending the HNSW graph with additional edges based on indexed payload values.
sources.use: Separates payload index, strategy selection and actual extra graph edges. Our exact candidate count is computed by enumerating/filtering scope, not a free cardinality estimate; our graph has no such payload-aware extra edges.
sources.version_limit: Live page redirected from concepts/indexing to manage-data/indexing. No latency or recall result is imported.
